summary.text: 视 means ‘look at’ or ‘see’ and is identified as the simplified form of 視. The earlier graph is interpreted as an eye above a standing figure; in the received form 視, 見 contributes the seeing-related meaning and 示 supplies a sound cue.

formation.text: The visible graph 视 is the simplified counterpart of 視. The received traditional form is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 見 contributes the seeing-related meaning and 示 is phonetic. Separately, an early form is interpreted as a whole picture of an eye above a standing person; this does not establish a sequence of component changes.

components.text: In the received graph 視, 見 is the semantic element associated with seeing. This analysis describes that traditional form and does not establish the structure of the proposed early pictograph.
In the received graph 視, 示 is analyzed as phonetic. The historical comparison is compatible with that analysis but does not by itself prove the component’s role.

sound_limitation.text: The reported Old Chinese forms share the rhyme and differ by the reconstructed *s- prefix, but this comparison does not prove 示’s graphic role. The modern Mandarin match likewise does not establish the ancient relationship.

sound.text: Baxter–Sagart’s reported Old Chinese forms for 示 and 視 share the rhyme and differ by the reconstructed *s- prefix, a comparison compatible with a phonetic relationship.

components.text: A proposed early form of 視 is interpreted as one picture of an eye above a standing figure. The curated image is a modern redraw, not an artifact image, and the reading remains a scholarly interpretation.

history.text: A paleographic interpretation distinguishes Shang oracle-bone graphs read as 視 and 見 by the figure below the eye: standing in the form read as 視, seated in 見. It also identifies standing-figure forms in Western Zhou bronzes and reports an early spelling using 見 and 氏 alongside the pictographic form. The curated oracle-style illustration is a modern redraw; an earlier reading of the standing-figure graph as 望 is reported and rejected.
The received traditional graph 視 is analyzed as 見 plus 示, with 見 semantic and 示 phonetic. The current character 视 is identified as the simplified form of 視.

uncertainties.text: The standing-figure reading is a scholarly interpretation, and individual archaic examples may remain disputed; no absolute date is supplied for a specific oracle-bone token. The supplied character accounts identify 视 as simplified from 視, though a character-specific official standard record was not retrieved.

示 is explicitly analyzed as phonetic in the traditional graph. The reported Baxter–Sagart comparison is compatible with that role, but reconstruction and current matching Mandarin readings do not independently prove the graphic analysis.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone evidence; individual token date unresolved
senses.text: The cited paleographic analysis identifies Shang oracle-bone contexts, including 視師 and 視方, as uses involving observing. The date of any individual token is not specified.

The received traditional graph is glossed as looking toward, and dictionary examples include examining or observing. When this use developed in relation to the basic looking or seeing sense is unresolved.
Current definitions include looking at, observing and seeing.

developments.text: Both uses are documented, but their chronological or derivational relationship is not established.

limitations.text: Other dictionary-attested uses include treating someone as, eyesight, caring for, administering, comparing, imitating, and a use glossed as 通「示」. Their chronology and connections are not established here.

components.text: 見 links the traditional graph to seeing.
示 is analyzed as the sound element in the traditional graph.
The proposed early graph is read as one picture: an eye above a standing person.

relationships.text: The supplied character accounts identify 视 as the simplified form of 視.
In the received traditional graph 視, 見 is the semantic element associated with seeing.

The received traditional analysis assigns 示 the phonetic role in 視. The reported Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese forms 示 *s-gijʔ-s and 視 *gijʔ-s share the rhyme and differ by the reconstructed *s- prefix, a comparison compatible with this analysis but not proof of the graphic role; their current Mandarin readings both match as shì.
